questions.q: A program that appears to be a free game but silently opens a backdoor for attackers is a:
questions.solution: The trojan's essence is disguise: useful-looking software that performs hidden malicious actions (backdoors, data theft). It does not self-replicate.
questions.shortcut: Looks useful, works evil = trojan horse.

questions.q: The browser shortcut to open a new tab is:
questions.solution: Ctrl+T opens a new tab; Ctrl+N a new window; Ctrl+W closes the current tab; Ctrl+Tab cycles through open tabs.
questions.shortcut: T = Tab, N = window. Ctrl+W wipes the tab.

questions.q: Which Office-wide shortcut opens the Font dialog box in PowerPoint?
questions.solution: Ctrl+T opens the Font dialog (face, style, size, effects) in PowerPoint. Ctrl+F is Find; Ctrl+D duplicates the selected slide/object.
questions.shortcut: In PPT, T = Type(faces): Ctrl+T is the font box.

questions.q: Which shortcut minimises all open windows to show the desktop, and restores them when pressed again?
questions.solution: Win+D toggles the desktop: the first press hides every window and the second press brings them back. Win+E opens File Explorer, and Win+Tab/Alt+Tab switch windows.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

You must obey the rules.
questions.solution: Modal row: **modal + be + V3** — 'The rules must be obeyed.' B uses V1; C uses 'been' after a modal (been only follows have/will have); D uses 'being' where plain 'be' is required.
questions.shortcut: Modal row: modal + be + V3 — no being, no been.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The retired professor could not put ___ with the constant construction noise.
questions.solution: Tolerate = **put up with**, a three-word unit whose object follows ('with the noise'). *Put on/off/in/across* build other meanings — wear, postpone, install, communicate.
questions.shortcut: Nuisance + 'could not' → tolerate → put up with.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

No sooner the bell rang / than the students / rushed out / of the classroom.
questions.solution: *No sooner* at the start requires inversion with an auxiliary: **No sooner did the bell ring** (or *No sooner had the bell rung*) *than...*. The rest is correct.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The captain, as well as / the players, were / congratulated by / the cricket board.
questions.solution: *As well as* does not build a plural subject; the verb follows the first subject, *the captain* → **was** congratulated. If the sentence meant both equally, it would use *and*.
questions.shortcut: 'As well as' is a intruder, not a conjunction of number — verb follows subject one.

questions.q: The **Partition of Bengal** (1905) was carried out by which Viceroy?
questions.solution: **Lord Curzon** announced the partition, which took effect on **16 October 1905** and triggered the Swadeshi movement. It was annulled in **1911** under Lord Hardinge.

questions.q: Megasthenes came to the court of Chandragupta Maurya as the ambassador of —
questions.solution: **Megasthenes** was sent by **Seleucus Nicator** after the treaty of 305 BCE and wrote ***Indica***. Deimachus came from **Antiochus I** to Bindusara's court.

questions.q: Vitamin K is essential for:
questions.solution: **Vitamin K** is needed to make clotting factors (such as prothrombin) in the liver; its deficiency leads to excessive bleeding. Vision needs vitamin A, gums need C, bones need D.

questions.q: The **Prayag Prashasti** inscribed on the Allahabad pillar, praising Samudragupta, was composed by —
questions.solution: **Harishena**, Samudragupta's court poet and minister, composed the Prayag Prashasti (Allahabad pillar, which also carries Ashokan edicts). It lists Samudragupta's campaigns in the north and the south.

questions.q: $\frac{3}{5}$ of a number is 63 more than $\frac{1}{4}$ of the number. What is the number?
questions.solution: $\left(\frac{3}{5} - \frac{1}{4}\right)x = 63 \Rightarrow \frac{7}{20}x = 63 \Rightarrow x = 180$.

questions.q: What is the unit digit of $17^{17^{17}}$?
questions.solution:
We need the exponent $17^{17}$ divided by 4. $17 = 4 \times 4 + 1$, so every power of 17 leaves remainder 1 with 4.
So $17^{17^{17}}$ ends like $7^1$ → **7**.

questions.q: What are the last two digits of $31^{786}$?
questions.shortcut: Base ends in 1: tens digit $= 3 \times 6 = 18 \to 8$; answer 81.

questions.q: A vessel contains 80 litres of pure milk. 8 litres are withdrawn and replaced with water. The ratio of milk to water in the vessel now is:
questions.solution: Milk left $= 72$ L, water $= 8$ L ⇒ $9 : 1$.

questions.q:
Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

**8 × 4 − 6 + 3 = 35**
questions.shortcut: Try the pair touching the last operator early — (6,3) — then confirm no earlier pair matched.
questions.pattern: fix the equation by swapping numbers

questions.q:
**Statements:** All villages are towns. Only a few towns are cities.

**Conclusions:** I. Some villages are cities. II. All villages being cities is a possibility.
questions.solution: I: the town-city overlap can sit entirely outside the villages → not forced. II: villages can be drawn inside the city-part of towns — consistent with 'only a few' (some towns stay outside cities) → possibility follows. **Only II.**
questions.shortcut: 'Only a few' says the city-part is small, never where your subject sits.

questions.q:
**Statements:** All cars are buses. Some trucks are buses.

**Conclusions:** I. Some cars are trucks. II. No car is a truck.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.solution: Cars sit inside buses, trucks somewhere in buses too — but the statements never fix whether cars meet trucks. I and II are exact negations of each other, so they cannot both fail. **Either-or.**
questions.shortcut: Same two terms, (Some …) vs (No …), neither provable → complementary pair.

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**3   4   13**

**5   2   11**

**6   3   ?**
questions.solution: Rule: third = first × second + 1. Check: 3×4 + 1 = 13 ✓; 5×2 + 1 = 11 ✓. So 6×3 + 1 = **19**. (18 is the bare product — the near-miss trap.)
questions.shortcut: Product first, then look for the small constant: +1 here.
questions.pattern: single grid, rows share a rule
